requirements.text: Append framed checksummed records before applying writes; acknowledge only at the selected sync boundary.
Recover a verified snapshot and contiguous WAL suffix, stopping only at a torn tail and rejecting interior corruption.
Publish checkpoints atomically with a cut LSN and retain WAL generations until the new manifest is durable.

problem.scope: Systems-coding design for a single-process in-memory key/value store. Compare synchronous per-write WAL with group commit and generation checkpoints. Physical power-loss guarantees depend on filesystem/device behavior and require fault injection beyond bounded reference models.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

acceptanceCases.given: A WAL record is appended but sync fails.
acceptanceCases.then: Fail the write acknowledgement and retain uncertainty; do not claim durable success.

acceptanceCases.given: A snapshot ends at LSN 2 and suffix contains 3,4 plus an incomplete tail.
acceptanceCases.then: Apply 3 and 4 once; stop at tail, but reject interior corruption or a sequence gap.
acceptanceCases.when: Replay with checksum and sequence validation.

evidence.testName: WAL framed suffix preserves tombstones rejects gaps and separates sync watermark

acceptanceCases.given: Snapshot cut is 2 with a key later deleted.
acceptanceCases.then: Preserve delete, stop at incomplete tail, reject checksum/gap, and release only waiters within the sync watermark; physical durability is untested.
acceptanceCases.when: Replay complete frames 3/4 and torn frame 5, then corrupt a frame and try a gap.

guarantees: A short write is retried or fails; it is never assumed complete.
OS-buffered append alone cannot satisfy always-sync acknowledgement.
The snapshot contains exactly state through its cut.
The old manifest and logs remain until publication is durable.
Interior checksum failure is a surfaced error, not skipped data.
No acknowledged suffix is removed before a recoverable checkpoint exists.
